when: 2026-08-04, taken on the tree that precedes the merge of PR #217
what: How much of a post-raid cohort's time was spent in the quarters and the tiles around them BEFORE the off-duty rule of Issue #201 existed. The 'after' file measures the same quantity with the same harness on the current tree; only the two together answer the owner's «все встали в больницу и не могли оттуда выйти».
theOwnersWords: разошлись быстрее, все встали в больницу и не могли оттуда выйти, возможно изза того что поле боя блокировало

base.what: Удар читается на экране (#210) (#218) — the commit immediately before 51302ba, which is the squash merge of PR #217
base.howObtained: git log --oneline -12 on origin/main; 51302ba is the merge of #217 and 4af03a5 is its parent
base.worktree: git worktree add --detach C:/gamedev/_wt-228-before 4af03a5, with tests/DungeonFortress.Simulation.Tests/PrototypeQuartersIdleTests.cs copied in from the branch of this issue and nothing else changed

howTheHarnessCarriesOver: PR #217 changed PrototypeWorld, PrototypeTuning, EventNarration and two test files and nothing in the snapshot schema (git diff --stat 4af03a5 51302ba). The harness reads only the published snapshot, so the same file compiles and measures the same quantity on both trees.

theWindowAndWhyItIsNotSixty.window: from the tick a wave ends to the tick the domain stops working: the start of the next muster (arriveTick - muster_lead_ticks), the arrival of the next wave, or WaveIntervalTicks = 350, whichever comes first
theWindowAndWhyItIsNotSixty.whyNotTheSixtyOf186And201: those two files measure the dispersal itself and 60 ticks is the right length for it — the last of the cohort is off the battlefield in 33. This issue measures what happens AFTER the walk, and the ninth creature does not begin walking until OffDutyDelayTicks + 8 * OffDutyStaggerTicks = 8 + 24 = 32 ticks have passed. A 60-tick window would end while the group is still arriving.
theWindowAndWhyItIsNotSixty.whyItStopsAtTheMuster: the correction independent review forced onto Issue #186: prepared sets muster_lead_ticks to 60 on tick 880, and a window that runs into the muster measures the muster, when the whole domain drops its work and walks into a Watch zone of ten tiles. Held by The_window_ends_before_the_domain_stops_working, which asserts that no tick of any window was spent by a creature with isMustering set.
theWindowAndWhyItIsNotSixty.cohort: everybody in CreatureMode.Fighting on the tick before the wave ended — the same cohort PrototypePostCombatDispersalTests and PrototypeOffDutyTests use, so the three files talk about the same people
theWindowAndWhyItIsNotSixty.place: the Quarters zone as the snapshot publishes it, plus every passable tile orthogonally adjacent to it and not in it ('и в тайлах вокруг них' of the issue)

perParty.note: prepared is identical on both trees, tick for tick and number for number, which is the cross-check that the whole change lives on baseline. Issue #201 measured why: the rule fires zero times on prepared, because that fixture paints a Watch zone and raises the Watch priority to 3, so there is standing work for everybody when a wave ends.

whyShareAndNotCount: the number of observed windows differs between the two trees (13 against 16) because the parties take a different course once creatures move — the same reason Issue #201 gave for reporting a share. Absolute counts of the two trees are not comparable and the shares are.
whatThisFileDoesNotClaim: that 9.1 % is a good number or that the tree before #217 was better. It is the reference the 'after' file is read against, and nothing else.
